The player awards 8/10 overall, praising simple controls, varied character attacks, mission objectives, and detailed graphics. They find the presentation somewhat cartoonish and wish for more cinematic storytelling. Having only the campaign limits the available modes, although the reviewer expects to enjoy repeating it.

This is a brief contemporary player review rather than a systematic technical assessment. The same review appears beneath GameFAQs’ Linux navigation, despite its 2003 date; that mirrored page is not evidence that the writer tested the Linux port.

## Detailed notes

Page facts: GameFAQs reader review "A Great Strategy game!" for Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood (PC); "Review by rios always" (handle rios_always); "Reviewed: 11/30/03"; rating "4.0 - Great" on GameFAQs' 5-point scale, with the reviewer's own overall score 8/10 in the text; the page also shows GameFAQs game details (Developer Spellbound, Publisher Strategy First, Release November 14, 2002, rated T, MetaCritic MetaScore 80 from 15 reviews, GameFAQs average user rating 3.76) and platform tabs for Linux and Macintosh. Retrieved from a Wayback Machine capture (the page markup carries a 2019 GameFAQs stylesheet and a 2019 CBS Interactive copyright; the exact capture timestamp is not preserved in the saved file). User-submitted commercial-site review, not transcribed.

Review content, in order:

- Describes the game as a real-time strategy game "from strategy first" featuring Robin Hood and the cast "from little John to maid Mary ann". Only a story mode is offered, "very good, but with a few flaws".
- Graphics 8/10: bird's-eye view; very detailed characters; "amazing" textures; "no frame lag at all"; characters look good zoomed in or out; only complaint is that they look "a bit too cartoony"; the game feels like Robin Hood's era.
- Gameplay 9/10: controls "truly great and not frustrating"; each character has different "attacks"; controls are so simple the beginning mini-tutorial is probably unnecessary; opponents react differently depending on how and from where they are hit; each mission's goals are "very original"; the game is fairly long and invites replaying; only drawback is a single mode.
- Storyline 7/10: "the real robin hood story", but the reviewer expected more cinematics; "nothing amazing, but nothing bad".
- Sound 8/10: character speeches are "original and funny"; effects "of the hood and all" are very good.
- Replay value 8/10: will last "a few good months"; the story mode may be restarted a few times.
- Rent or buy: any real-time strategy fan should check it out; non-fans should rent; price cited as "30 dollars big maximum".
- Overall 8/10; closing line "a game for a true hero!"

Header note: the same review is reachable under GameFAQs' Linux and Macintosh product pages via the platform tabs; nothing in the text indicates which platform the writer used.
